body: Renaming the name of the blender node (and not the mesh data) to have the "-colonly" suffix works. e.g. this is imported correctly as [The docs](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.1/tutorials/assets_pipeline/importing_scenes.html#create-collisions-col-convcol-colonly-convcolonly) state: > The option -col will work only for Mesh objects. And based on the rest of that section its believable that this would also be true of -colonly, as the option is modifying the mesh (by deleting and replacing it): > To solve this, the -colonly modifier exists. It will remove the mesh... What's unusual here is that -col _does_ also seem to be working when suffix-ing the mesh data (so the statement about -col only working for mesh objects seems false). --- Just to be clear I believe the blender terminology is this:

After a little more digging this is my conclusion:

| Suffix       | Works on MeshObject | Works on MeshData |
|--------------|---------------------|-------------------|
| -col         | ✅                   | ✅                 |
| -convcol     | ✅                   | ✅                 |
| -colonly     | ✅                   | ❌                 |
| -convcolonly | ✅                   | ❌                 |

suffixing meshobjects vs meshdata with -col or -convcol looks to be indistinguishable (from a brief test).

Apologies, I wasn't sure of the correct Blender terminology, the terms "node" and "mesh" are used internally in your importer code, so I went with those.

Anyway, my issue isn't that the documentation is misleading, but the behaviour is inconsistent.

> What's unusual here is that -col does also seem to be working when suffix-ing the mesh data (so the statement about -col only working for mesh objects seems false).

As mentioned in my "Issue Description" this is because the existing engine code performs an additional set of checks specifically on the MeshData name to handle '-col' and '-convcol' from there, but it doesn't do this for '-colonly' or '-convcolonly'.

I suspect this is an oversight as it would be useful if the engine did this additional check for all cases.

In the case of my particular problem, I don't have control over the MeshObject names in Blender as I'm using Geometry Nodes to generate them, but I do have some control over the MeshData name, so for that reason it would be really useful if the engine dealt with all of these suffixes in a consistent manner and could pick them up from the MeshData name.
